first_step_test: One small head joins a long S-curved neck in its final upright position. This connected gesture fixes the heron's distinctive height and direction before the larger body and legs arrive.

source.notes: Planned six-panel cumulative graphite and restrained colored-pencil contact sheet for the September 10 current lesson. No temporary guides; preserve rejected iterations privately.

final_elements.description: Small left-facing head connected to one long S-curved neck in its final position.

final_elements.name: body and short tail
final_elements.description: One long oval body attached behind the neck with a short pointed tail.

final_elements.name: near leg
final_elements.description: Long near leg descending from the lower body to a foot with three forward toes and one rear toe.

final_elements.description: Second long leg offset behind the near leg with three forward toes and one rear toe.

frames.visible_job: Draw one small left-facing head and continue its lower edge into a long S-curved neck, then return along the back of the neck and stop above the shoulder opening.
frames.instruction: Draw one small left-facing head and continue its lower edge into a long S-curved neck. Return along the back of the neck and stop above the shoulder opening, leaving room to attach the body on the right.

frames.visible_job: Attach one long oval body and short pointed tail behind the neck, then drop two narrow legs from separate lower-body anchors and divide each foot into three forward toes and one rear toe.
frames.instruction: Attach one long oval body and a short pointed tail behind the neck. From two separate points under the body, drop the near leg straight down and the far leg slightly back; split each foot into three forward toes and one rear toe.

frames.visible_job: Extend a long pointed beak from the head, add one small eye, and sweep one dark tapered crown stripe behind it.
frames.instruction: From the front of the head, pull two tapering lines left into one long pointed beak. Place one small dark eye above the beak base and sweep one tapered crown stripe from above the eye toward the back of the head.

frames.visible_job: Draw one folded wing inside the body with three long feather groups and add a short broken feather edge down the chest.
frames.instruction: Inside the body, draw one folded wing that follows the back and tapers toward the tail. Divide its lower half into three long feather groups, then add a short broken feather edge down the lower neck and chest.

frames.visible_job: Add two tall reeds behind the bird, one shorter reed beside the legs, and exactly three short horizontal ripple marks around the feet.
frames.instruction: Raise one tall reed behind each side of the heron and a shorter center reed beside the legs, stopping every background line at the bird. Give each reed one narrow leaf, then draw exactly three short horizontal ripple marks around the feet without covering the toes.

final_step.visible_job: Add graphite value and restrained blue-gray, ochre, muted green, and pale blue within the established contours.
final_step.instruction: Layer blue-gray pencil over the body and folded wing, warm ochre on the established beak and legs, muted green on the three reeds, and pale blue through the three ripple marks. Deepen the crown stripe and feather shadows with graphite while leaving paper highlights visible and adding no new contours.
adds: graphite value and restrained blue-gray ochre green and pale-blue color

visual_review.first_step_observation: The first saved crop contains only one small left-facing head joined to one long upright S-neck. Its open shoulder ends leave a clear attachment point for the body, and no later wing, leg, reed, or water detail appears early.
visual_review.draw_through_observation: Read all six final instructions while comparing every saved adjacent pair. The head and neck, two leg anchors, eight toes, beak, eye, crown stripe, three wing groups, chest edge, three reeds with leaves, and three single ripples stay fixed; the finish adds color and graphite value without new structure.
